finding: src/anomaly/readme.py:36 README projection can delete journalist-authored Markdown that happens to equal the legacy Outputs block.
rationale: The public workflow reaches this projection on P7 completion, completed-case resume, and P7 invalidation, and no upstream content guard prevents a journalist-authored block from exactly matching _OUTPUTS, so the global replacement can delete valid authored Markdown and the medium data-loss severity is honest.

evidence.output: project_readme reads the existing README, removes the bounded anomaly marker block, then calls .replace(_OUTPUTS, "") without a count or marker requirement; the only local guards are README existence and non-symlink status.

run_workflow calls load_snapshot on a real case; load_snapshot projects completed P7 READMEs, _invalidate_state projects after invalidating a previously completed P7 case, and _seal_success projects after successful P7 completion.
The only README content mutation/guard in production is readme.py; no validator rejects or distinguishes an unmarked journalist-authored exact _OUTPUTS block.
Acceptance explicitly requires README projection to preserve journalist-authored content, making deletion of a valid unmarked matching section a contract violation.
